section: India - population growth: decadal trends, growth rate, Census 2011 highlights
subsections: Decadal trends - phases of growth and the year of great divide
Census history - first census, first synchronous census, number
Components of growth - natural increase and migration
Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s: Which one of the following periods is associated with the stagnant or stationary phase of India's population growth?
accepted.x: The stagnant or stationary phase extended from 1901 to 1921 and was characterised by high birth and death rates.
accepted.tq: Use the phase–period association and eliminate periods belonging to later phases.
accepted.sec: Decadal trends - phases of growth and the year of great divide

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the phases of India's population growth:
1. The period 1951–1981 witnessed a rapid decline in mortality while fertility remained high.
2. The average annual growth during the population-explosion phase was about 2.2 percent.
3. Migration from Tibet, Bangladesh, Nepal and Pakistan was associated with the population-explosion phase.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the population-explosion phase of 1951–1981.
accepted.tq: Combine several features of one phase and test them through coded statements.
accepted.sec: Decadal trends - phases of growth and the year of great divide

accepted.s:
The slowdown or high-but-declining phase of India's population growth is associated with which of the following factors?
1. Later marriage
2. Female education
3. Decline in the crude birth rate
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: After 1981, later marriage and female education contributed to a fall in the crude birth rate, producing a high-but-declining growth phase.
accepted.tq: Test cause-and-effect links through an all-inclusive coded option.
accepted.sec: Decadal trends - phases of growth and the year of great divide

accepted.s: Which year is known as the “Year of the Great Divide” in the demographic history of India?
accepted.x: The year 1921 is called the Year of the Great Divide because it marked the only census period showing a decline in India's population.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of a standard demographic landmark year.
accepted.sec: Decadal trends - phases of growth and the year of great divide

accepted.s:
The decline in India's population during 1911–1921 was associated with which of the following?
1. Influenza pandemic
2. Famines
3. A sustained decline in population after 1921
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The decline during 1911–1921 was associated with the influenza pandemic and famines. After 1921, India's population increased in every decade.
accepted.tq: Find the false statement created by reversing the post-1921 trend.
accepted.sec: Decadal trends - phases of growth and the year of great divide

accepted.s:
Arrange the following census years in chronological order of the decadal population growth figures given for them:
A. 1951 – 13.31 percent
B. 2011 – 17.64 percent
C. 1971 – 24.80 percent
D. 2001 – 21.54 percent
accepted.x: The chronological order is 1951, 1971, 2001 and 2011; their recorded growth figures were 13.31, 24.80, 21.54 and 17.64 percent respectively.
accepted.tq: First arrange the census years, then verify the attached figures.
accepted.sec: Decadal trends - phases of growth and the year of great divide

accepted.s: India recorded its peak decadal population growth of 24.80 percent during which period?
accepted.x: The peak decadal growth rate was 24.80 percent during 1961–1971, often described as the explosion decade in the relevant classification.
accepted.tq: Match the peak percentage with its corresponding decade.
accepted.sec: Decadal trends - phases of growth and the year of great divide

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The population recorded for 1901 was 23.84 crore. The other figures are mismatched: 1951 had 36.11 crore, 1971 had 54.82 crore and 2011 had 121.02 crore.
accepted.tq: Check each population figure against its census year to identify the correctly matched pair.
accepted.sec: Decadal trends - phases of growth and the year of great divide

accepted.s: The annual compound growth rate of India's population was about 0.19 percent during 1891–1921 and rose subsequently to approximately:
accepted.x: The annual compound growth rate rose from about 0.19 percent during 1891–1921 to approximately 2.15 percent in the later period.
accepted.tq: Use the two-point numerical comparison rather than the decadal-growth figures.
accepted.sec: Decadal trends - phases of growth and the year of great divide

accepted.s: The first population census in India was conducted in 1872 under the administration of:
accepted.x: The first census was conducted in 1872 under Lord Mayo and was non-synchronous.
accepted.tq: Apply the who-and-when recall pattern to distinguish the two early censuses.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, first synchronous census, number

accepted.s:
Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the censuses of 1872 and 1881?
1. The 1872 census was non-synchronous.
2. The 1881 census was the first complete and synchronous census.
3. Lord Ripon was associated with the 1881 census.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The 1872 census was non-synchronous, whereas the 1881 census was the first complete and synchronous census and was conducted under Lord Ripon.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two easily confused census years and their associated viceroys.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, first synchronous census, number

accepted.s: Census operations in India have been conducted on a decennial basis since:
accepted.x: Regular decennial census operations began with the first complete and synchronous census of 1881.
accepted.tq: Separate the first census from the beginning of the regular decennial series.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, first synchronous census, number

accepted.s: Census 2011 was the:
o: 15th census of India and 7th after Independence
14th census of India and 6th after Independence
16th census of India and 7th after Independence
15th census of India and 8th after Independence
accepted.x: Census 2011 was the 15th census of India and the 7th census conducted after Independence.
accepted.tq: Test two related counts together to prevent confusion between total and post-Independence series.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, first synchronous census, number

accepted.s: The reference date for Census 2011 was:
accepted.x: The reference date for Census 2011 was 1 March 2011.
accepted.tq: Numerical date discrimination among adjacent census months.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, first synchronous census, number

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly states the legal and constitutional basis of population census in India?
1. Census Act, 1948
2. Union List Entry 69
3. Article 246 of the Constitution
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948, and census matters fall under Union List Entry 69 within the constitutional framework of Article 246.
accepted.tq: Combine statutory and constitutional references in a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, first synchronous census, number

accepted.s: The population census in India is conducted by the:
o: Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Public Service Commission under the Ministry of Personnel
NITI Aayog under the Ministry of Statistics
accepted.x: The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, conducts and administers the census.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-authority trap by distinguishing the responsible body from neighbouring agencies.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, first synchronous census, number

accepted.s: Natural increase in population refers to:
accepted.x: Natural increase is the difference between the number of births and the number of deaths; migration is not included in this component.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between natural increase and actual population growth.
accepted.sec: Components of growth - natural increase and migration

accepted.s: A population is likely to record positive growth when:
o: Births and deaths are equal irrespective of migration
Deaths exceed births and out-migration is permanent
Births exceed deaths or there is permanent net in-migration
accepted.x: Positive growth occurs when births exceed deaths or when permanent net in-migration adds to the population.
accepted.tq: Apply the natural-increase and migration conditions to a demographic situation.
accepted.sec: Components of growth - natural increase and migration

accepted.s: According to the stated SRS 2024 figure, India's natural growth rate was:
accepted.x: The SRS 2024 natural growth rate was 11.9 per 1,000 population.
accepted.tq: Directly distinguish the reported rate from nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Components of growth - natural increase and migration

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Census 2027 is correct?
o: It will be India's first paper-only census after Independence.
It will exclude all caste-related questions.
It will be the first digital census and will use mobile applications and self-enumeration.
It was scheduled to precede Census 2011.
accepted.x: Census 2027 is planned as India's first digital census, using mobile applications and a self-enumeration facility.
accepted.tq: Use the official feature of the upcoming census against reversed or absolute alternatives.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s: Census 2027 is significant for caste enumeration because it will:
o: conduct the first caste count in independent India beyond Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
enumerate caste only in urban areas
abolish enumeration of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
count only Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
accepted.x: Census 2027 is intended to undertake the first caste enumeration in independent India beyond the existing Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe enumeration.
accepted.tq: Test the precise scope of a policy announcement using confusable alternatives.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the phases of Census 2027:
1. House Listing and Housing Census is scheduled for April–September 2026.
2. Population Enumeration is scheduled for February 2027.
3. The reference date for the regular population enumeration is 1 March 2027.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: House Listing and Housing Census is planned for April–September 2026, followed by Population Enumeration in February 2027, with 1 March 2027 as the reference date.
accepted.tq: Combine phase, timing and reference-date facts in one coded question.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s: In the snow-bound areas of Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, Census 2027 enumeration is scheduled during:
o: 1 April–30 September 2026, with reference date 1 March 2027
17 August–30 September 2026, with reference date 1 October 2026
1 January–28 February 2027, with reference date 1 March 2027
1 October–31 December 2026, with reference date 1 January 2027
accepted.x: Enumeration in the snow-bound areas is scheduled for 17 August–30 September 2026, using 1 October 2026 as the reference date.
accepted.tq: Discriminate a special regional schedule from the general census schedule.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s: How many questions were notified for Census 2027, and how many of them were new compared with Census 2011?
accepted.x: Forty questions were notified for Census 2027, including 13 new questions; Census 2011 had 29 questions.
accepted.tq: Pair two related figures and reject options that swap or alter one number.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a feature of the caste-related question proposed for Census 2027?
o: A question restricted to migration history
A column applicable only to foreign citizens
A closed list containing only Scheduled Castes
accepted.x: The proposed caste question includes an open-ended caste column.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise administrative feature rather than the broad policy objective.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s: Who is identified as the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India for Census 2027?
accepted.x: Mritunjay Kumar Narayan is identified as the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.
accepted.tq: Use the exact office-holder against historically associated and look-alike names.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s:
Population Enumeration for Census 2027 was advanced in which of the following poll-bound States, while it was deferred in Manipur?
1. Uttar Pradesh
2. Punjab
3. Uttarakhand
4. Goa
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Population Enumeration was advanced in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Goa, while it was deferred in Manipur.
accepted.tq: Test a complete geographical list through an all-inclusive option.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s: Approximately how many enumerators are associated with Census 2027?
accepted.x: Approximately 34 lakh enumerators are associated with the Census 2027 exercise.
accepted.tq: Direct numerical recall with evenly spaced lakh-based distractors.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s:
Census 2027 is intended to provide the population base for which of the following?
1. Delimitation
2. Women's reservation
3. Replacement of the Census Act, 1948
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Census 2027 will provide the population base for delimitation and women's reservation. It does not replace the Census Act, 1948.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated legal proposition among two connected policy uses.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the postponement and scheduling of India's recent census operations?
o: Census 2021 was completed digitally and the next census is Census 2026.
Census 2021 was postponed because of COVID-19 and the next census is Census 2027.
Census 2027 was postponed because of COVID-19 and the next census is Census 2031.
Census 2011 was postponed because of COVID-19 and the next census is Census 2021.
accepted.x: Census 2021 was postponed because of the COVID-19 pandemic, and the next census is scheduled as Census 2027.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the postponed census year from the announced next census year.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s:
With reference to the constitutional provisions connected with Census 2027, consider the following statements:
1. The 84th Amendment is associated with the freeze on delimitation until the first census after 2026.
2. The 106th Amendment is associated with women's reservation.
3. Article 334A is connected with the women's reservation framework.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 84th Amendment is linked to the delimitation freeze, while the 106th Amendment and Article 334A are linked to the framework for women's reservation.
accepted.tq: Match each constitutional reference with its correct policy consequence.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s:
A settlement will qualify as a Census Town under the stated criteria only if it has:
1. Population of at least 5,000
2. At least 75 percent of male workers engaged outside agriculture
3. Population density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: A Census Town is a village-status settlement meeting all three criteria: population of at least 5,000, at least 75 percent of male workers outside agriculture, and density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre.
accepted.tq: Apply all threshold conditions to classify a settlement.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding the Census Town criteria and status?
o: Male workers outside agriculture — At least 50 percent
Density threshold — At least 400 persons per square kilometre
accepted.x: The required proportion of male workers engaged outside agriculture is at least 75 percent, not 50 percent. The other three descriptions are correct.
accepted.tq: Find the altered threshold in a list of closely related criteria.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census

accepted.s: Which statement best reflects the position of Census Towns for Census 2027?
o: The Registrar General of India will discontinue the Census Town category completely.
The category will be converted into a statutory municipality in every case.
The category has been unchanged since 1951 and is accepted without criticism.
The Registrar General of India will retain the category, although the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs regards it as outdated.
accepted.x: The Registrar General of India is expected to retain the Census Town category for Census 2027, although the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs considers it outdated because of male bias and uniform thresholds.
accepted.tq: Separate the administrative decision to retain a category from the criticism of its criteria.
accepted.sec: Upcoming Census - caste enumeration and digital census
